options: Attempts to detect and clean up messy spreadsheet layouts — merged titles, multiple sub-tables, spacer rows
Automatically writes calculated fields for you
Converts a Live connection into an Extract
Translates field names into another language
questions.explain: Data Interpreter targets human-formatted spreadsheets — title rows, multiple stacked tables, blank spacers — and tries to isolate the real data, flagging what it excluded.

questions.q: What does the Split transformation do to a field like 'Customer Name' containing 'Claire Gute'?
options: Breaks it into multiple new fields based on a detected or specified delimiter, e.g. into separate first- and last-name columns
Deletes the field entirely
Converts it from a Dimension into a Measure
Merges it with another field
questions.explain: Split (automatic or custom) divides one field into multiple fields using a delimiter like a space or comma.

questions.q: What does Pivot do when applied to a wide table with one column per brand (Samsung, Nokia, Apple)?
options: Turns those columns into rows — creating a 'Pivot Field Names' column (the brand) and a 'Pivot Field Values' column (the number)
Deletes all but one brand's column
Automatically renames the brand columns
Converts the table into a Live connection
questions.explain: Pivot reshapes selected columns into two new columns: one holding the former column names, one holding their values — turning wide data long.

questions.q: What does a NULL value actually represent?
options: A genuinely missing/absent value — distinct from zero or an empty text string
The number zero, formatted differently
An error in the Tableau software
A value that has been explicitly filtered out by the user
questions.explain: NULL means no value was recorded at all — it's not the same as zero or blank text, and needs to be handled deliberately in calculations.

questions.q: Why can NULL values be dangerous inside a calculation if not handled?
options: An operation involving NULL (like NULL + 5) typically returns NULL itself, which can silently affect results rather than raising a visible error
NULLs always cause Tableau to crash immediately
NULLs are automatically converted to the string 'NULL' in every calculation
NULLs cannot exist inside any calculated field, so this is not actually a concern
questions.explain: Arithmetic involving NULL tends to silently propagate as NULL rather than throwing an error, which is why functions like IFNULL()/ZN() exist to substitute defaults.
